newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway c.bank chief warns against weakened budget.
newsitem.headline: Norway c.bank chief warns against weakened budget.

text.p: Norway's central bank governor Kjell Storvik said on Monday any weakening of the 1997 state budget would be detrimental to balanced economic development.

Storvik, asked by reporters about efforts by the opposition in parliament to increase expenditure, said the central bank had wanted an even tighter budget for 1997 than was presented by the government on October 4.
"Every weakening of the budget balance would be unfortunate for the main point of bringing about a balanced economic development," he said.
News reports at the weekend said a majority in parliament wanted to raise spending in the 1997 budget by 6.8 billion crowns partly through higher welfare payments.

Oil-rich Norway's draft budget envisages a 40.9 billion crown surplus. Despite the surplus projected for next year, the government has said it will keep a tight grip on purse strings for fear of fuelling inflation.

Storvik has previously urged parlament not to dilute the budget and said he shared the government's view that there was a clear risk of further pressure on the economy and higher cost growth next year.
The Labour minority government is under pressure from the opposition right and left of centre to increase expenditure before the budget is finally adopted in December.
